title: Transient electric discharge across oil film
body:
I am a mechanical engineer researching electric discharge damage in rolling-element bearings. I have a rig that runs a simplified single-contact lubricated contact (simulating a bearing contact). Across the lubricated ball-disc steel contact, I apply an external electric potential with a series resistor to control maximum current flow across the contact. The context is similar to Electric Discharge Machining (EDM), which can accidentally occur in bearings. The oil film between the contact has a certain breakdown voltage and permittivity. As per the literature, the oil film acts as a capacitor and a resistor in parallel. The applied voltage across the oil film results in a dielectric strength exceeding the breakdown voltage of the oil, so breakdown and discharges occur. I study DC voltage (18V), square wave AC voltage (+/- 18V, 10 kHz) and pulse voltage (18V, 10 kHz, pulse duration 10 microseconds). I have attached a schematic of the setup.

With either DC or AC, I observe longer-duration (approximately 100 microseconds) discharge signals instead of instantaneous capacitive discharge. At first, I thought it was a continuously sustained arc discharge, but similar behaviour during AC suggests otherwise. I don't have a capacitor in the circuit, but I suspect there would be some capacitance from the rig and wiring. I observe discharge damage on the steel surfaces (craters formed by melting and resolidified splash features), typical of discharge damage. Reducing the maximum current limit, I still observe the discharges but not the damage, suggesting the energy is reduced to form the craters. I have attached images of the signals acquired during the tests.

My question is what could be the physics behind longer-duration breakdowns instead of instantaneous capacitive discharge? The energy calculated to form the observed discharge craters is 1000s of magnitude less than the calculated energy from such a long breakdown pulse. And why does the current measurement during DC voltage tests show a current peak exceeding the maximum current limit set?

title: Making a Bicycle Hybrid
body:
I'm out of my depth and need help to guide my high-school students.

They are working on a project where they're modifying a normal bike to make it a hybrid one. The kits I've seen in the market are for making a bike fully electric and needing to charge through electricity, not a hybrid one. The plan is to have a switch that allows you toggle between drawing power from the battery to power the motor and charging the battery through the motor.

The original idea came from a student who did this two years ago, installed the motor with one battery, added a buck-booster and a diode in the circuit. His original design worked in theory, but it was rushed together at the end where breadboard and circuit part were taped to the body of the bike in a way that didn't allow for proper testing if it actually worked in terms of charging the battery.

This year, I allowed one student to adopt this and take from a proof of concept to a functional prototype. He already installed a 250 W 24 V motor to the rear in the opposite side of normal gears and connected to two 12 V 9 Ah lead acid batteries (welding this on the opposite side of the pedal ensures the motor is rotating when one is going down hill to generate power). The student tried to blindly follow last year's circuit design but it fell short in the end.

Is this even feasible? How can you build the circuit to toggle between the modes mentioned above?

title: Algorithm to authenticate between a PC GUI software and Controller board
body:
I am developing a front end GUI software using python which communicates with a slave controller using RS485. I write software for both the front end and the slave controller. There is a requirement that the front end software should not be misused, that is even if someone gets access to the GUI executable, he should not be able to communicate with the slave board. The main aim is:

  • The persons who are authorized to use both the GUI and slave hardware can use it;
  • Others should not be able to use the software at all with no functionality.

I am confused and request recommendations on what kind of security and how many levels of algorithms I have to develop.

title: Simple KVL 2-loop problem with outer loop equation
body:
I have come across many instances where the proposed solution for a 2-loop KVL system uses three loop equations: 2 small loops and 1 large outer loop. I have never been able to make this work. In addition, some sources indicate that in general when solving this type of problem using KVL/KCL (not mesh or node) you can only get a number of equations equal to the number of open loops in the circuit diagram; which does not include the outer loop because it is not open. The same source indicates that it is usual to obtain the third equation using KCL at a node. This always works.

A typical example of what does not work comes from a different source as follows

The following solution obtains the correct values

Loop A $$ I_1 + 2I_3 = 1 $$ Loop B $$ 3 I_2 + 4I_3 = 3$$
Node 1 $$ I_1 + I_2 - I_3 = 0 $$ Yields the following correct solutions $$ I_1 = 77mA $$ $$ I_2 = 385mA $$ $$ I_3 = 462mA $$

However when using KVL at Loop C instead of the Node 1 KCL equation we obtain infinitely many solutions which includes the correct set above. Is this an error to attempt to use three loop equations in a 2-loop circuit such as this? Presumably the reason for this is that one must have at least one equation which includes all three variables.

title: How to connect a backup battery automatically when primary battery is below a threshold voltage
body:
I have cameras that have 10,000mAh rechargeable battery (rechargeable either via solar panel or DC 5V 2A adaptor). My use case is that I need to install them in vehicles on trip basis (4 days trip) and it is hundreds of trips and cameras. I cannot use solar panel to charge it as I had cases where drivers threw them away.

As a solution, I will place a backup battery (12V 5A SLA) with buck converter somewhere in the vehicle which will connect to the power input side of the camera. But it should only get connected if the internal battery falls below 3.6V.

You might say that a microcontroller can be used to monitor the camera battery voltage and when it goes down the threshold then It activates a relay which connects the 12V 5A battery with the input side of the camera. But because we have 100s of vehicles and trips per month, this solution is not viable and managing microcontrollers is difficult as well on vehicles.

I am looking to do this task using a circuit. Once the backup battery is connected to camera input, I do not need anymore voltage monitoring because the backup can provide enough power to complete the trip as I know camera battery can cover 40-60% of the trip.
